answer: Each agent identity must lock a stake that unlocks only after a withdrawal delay from the last dawn, and peer-attested fraud burns the bond plus a penalty. A jetty of escrowed capital therefore blocks instant exit, while one crystal-clear invalid action can slash all linked stakes. To mint many identities, an attacker must fund each bond and keep it exposed through delay and slashing, so sybil cost scales with locked capital, not free registrations.
